[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
James was born in 1740. The existing attachment to [[Glasgow-2988|James Glasgow]] as father is retained as an '''uncertain working relationship'''; no reviewed source names his father.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-2988]] is assessed at 19% (uncertain). Two 1766 Drumearn James householders permit an older/younger model, but neither is identified with 2988/2989 and no ages or kin are given. The profile dates partly encode the hypothesis itself.

Complete selected father-profile proposition; recorded role and adult identification distinguished below.

Next useful test: Find a lease or testament with both James men and explicit kin.

Source basis already held: [https://virtualtreasury.ie/item/NAI-IHP-1-665 National Archives of Ireland, Parliamentary Return 665, 1766 religious census for Derryloran, IHP/1/665, original return and transcription (https://virtualtreasury.ie/item/NAI-IHP-1-665), accessed 17 July 2026; independently transcribed in RCB Library MS 23, pp. 162–163.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



The original 1766 Derryloran religious return lists '''two''' James Glasgow householders at Drumearn, each written as ''Jams Glasco''. It also lists John Glasco at Drumearn, Samuel Glasco at Gortein, and William Glasco at Killycurry.<ref>National Archives of Ireland, Parliamentary Return 665, 1766 religious census for Derryloran, IHP/1/665, [https://virtualtreasury.ie/item/NAI-IHP-1-665 original return and transcription], accessed 17 July 2026; independently transcribed in RCB Library MS 23, pp. 162–163.</ref>

The return proves a substantial local Glasgow cluster, but gives no ages or relationships. It does not identify which of the two Drumearn men, if either, is this profile, and it does not establish Glasgow-2988 as his father. The two contemporary same-name householders must not be conflated.

=== Drumeen probate candidates ===
Probate indexes name James Glasgow of Drumeen in 1820 and James Glasgow, farmer, of Drumeen in 1822. The entries may represent this James, two men, or other local namesakes; neither surviving index entry states a relationship that identifies this profile.<ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx Underlying record source: james glasgow drumeen 1820].</ref><ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx Underlying record source: james glasgow drumeen farmer 1822].</ref>
